disposition_reason: Original ICP measurements of trace elements and heavy metals in retail broiler meat, chicken burger, frankfurter, liver and table eggs in Jeddah.

study.design: Retail market survey of chicken meat, meat products, liver and table eggs, plus farm feed and litter
study.origin: Fresh carcasses and products from three Saudi brands; frozen carcasses imported from Brazil, France and USA; eggs from four Saudi brands
study.market: Retail market, Jeddah City, Saudi Arabia
study.method: ICP-OES (Varian 720-ES) after HNO3/H2SO4 digestion of oven-dried samples (text also refers to ICP-MS protocols)
study.qa: No CRM or recovery data reported; method said to be validated by CSL for foods

controls.outcome: Pb UDL (meat) -> 16.69 (burger) and 14.84 ppm DM (frankfurter); Cd UDL -> 0.433 and 0.379 ppm; Ni UDL -> 7.10 and 7.28 ppm

controls.control: Imported frozen vs locally produced fresh carcass
controls.outcome: Pb, Cd, As, Ni undetectable in both; Cr 7.01 (frozen) vs 9.75 ppm DM (fresh)

unresolved: Sample numbers for burger, frankfurter and liver are given only as 45 samples in total; per-product n not stated.
Feed and litter results (Tables 1-4) are not food findings.
Methods name ICP-OES for analysis but then describe ICP-MS operating protocols.
Numeric detection limits for UDL entries are not reported.
Table 7 burger, frankfurter and liver columns repeat Table 5 values and were not extracted twice; Table 7 liver lead is 16.52 vs 16.51 ppm in Table 5.
Lead of about 15-17 ppm dry matter in burger, frankfurter and liver is unusually high; no QA data support it.
Table 7 pooled meat copper is printed UDL although Table 5 prints 0.036 and 0.056 ppm for frozen and fresh meat.
